threads.thread_goal: Align on target account list and pilot scope for the new device program.

messages.text: Hi team, we're kicking off the new medical device education and sales program. We have 21 days to get the pilot ready. First priority: we need to lock down our target account list and decide which hospitals and clinics we'll focus on initially. I've started a rough list but want input from everyone on which accounts are most receptive and where we have existing relationships. Let's use A1 (Target Account Segmentation Sheet) to build this out together. Who can help prioritise by region and specialty?

I can start mapping out the accounts I know best. We should focus on the major teaching hospitals first—they tend to be early adopters and can influence smaller clinics. I'm thinking we target maybe 8-10 accounts for the pilot wave. Let me pull together what I have on existing relationships and decision-makers.

Good idea on the teaching hospitals. I have contacts at three major centres in the region. Should we also include some mid-size private clinics? They might move faster on adoption. I can help fill in the details once we agree on the criteria.
I'll get the account data from our CRM and start populating the sheet. We should probably tier them by size and current engagement level. Let me know what fields you want me to include.

From an education perspective, I'd suggest we also consider which accounts have active clinical education committees or regular grand rounds. Those venues are perfect for introducing the device. Once we have the list, I can help tailor the webinar topics to each account's specialty mix.

Good. Include account name, region, specialty, current relationship status, key contacts and estimated decision timeline. That'll help us prioritise. Let's aim to have the first draft of A1 ready by EOD tomorrow so we can review and decide on the pilot scope.

I'll send over my account notes by end of day. One question though—should we weight the list toward accounts where we already have strong clinical champions, or should we try to build new relationships? I think champions matter more for adoption.

Champions are critical. If we have existing clinical champions at an account, that's a huge advantage. They can help us navigate the institution and get buy-in from peers. I'd prioritise those accounts first.
Agreed. I'll flag which of my contacts are strong advocates. That should help us narrow down the list quickly.
Let's plan a quick sync tomorrow afternoon once we have the draft sheet. We'll review the accounts, confirm the priority tiers, and lock in which ones make the first pilot wave. That'll be D1 and D2.
I'll have the sheet ready by 2pm tomorrow. Should be straightforward to pull from the CRM.
Works for me. I'll have my notes compiled by then.
Perfect. I'll review the list from an education angle and come with suggestions on which accounts align best with our webinar strategy.
Ready to go. See you tomorrow.
Great. Let's aim for 3pm tomorrow in the sync. I'll send the calendar invite now.

Just uploaded the first draft of A1 to the shared drive. It has 12 accounts across three regions. I've flagged the ones with existing relationships. Let me know if you need any adjustments to the data.

Good work. I've reviewed it and added notes on the clinical champions at each site. I think we should narrow this to 8 accounts for the pilot—the ones with the strongest relationships and most receptive decision-makers. That keeps us focused and manageable.

I've reviewed the list too. Eight accounts works well from an education standpoint. I can design webinar topics that fit each account's specialty mix. The teaching hospitals and the two private clinics with strong champions are my top picks.
I agree with eight. Keeps us lean and lets us really focus on execution. I've confirmed availability with my three contacts—they're all interested in learning more about the device.

Excellent. So we're aligned: 8 accounts for the pilot wave, prioritised by existing relationships and clinical champions. I'm marking D1 (approve initial list and priority tiers) and D2 (confirm pilot wave size) as decided. Let me update A1 with the final eight and assign owners to each account.
I'll update the CRM to flag these eight accounts as pilot targets. That way we can track all interactions in one place.
Perfect. Now that we have the target list locked, I can start drafting the educational slide deck. I'll have a first version ready by end of week for feedback. That ties into T2.
Good. Once you have the deck, I can start working on the sales script and objection guide. We'll need those aligned before we start any calls.

Agreed. Let's plan to have the deck and script ready for regulatory review by mid-week. That gives us time to incorporate feedback before the pilot kicks off. I'll coordinate with the regulatory affairs team.

threads.thread_goal: Review and finalise educational slide deck and sales script.

messages.text: I've drafted the clinician-focused educational slide deck for the new device. It covers indications, mechanism of action, clinical benefits and safety information. All claims are sourced from approved clinical data. I'd like feedback from the sales team on whether the messaging resonates and if there are any objections we should address upfront. The deck is in A2. Please review and comment.

Thanks for getting this out quickly. I've reviewed it and the structure is solid. The clinical data is clear and the benefits section is compelling. One question: do we have slides on contraindications and patient selection criteria? That's usually a key question from clinicians.

Good catch. I have a slide on contraindications but it's brief. Let me expand that section with more detail on patient selection criteria and any populations where the device is not recommended. That's critical for clinician credibility.

I've looked at the deck. The mechanism slide is really clear—that's good because clinicians always want to understand how it works. One thing: I'd suggest adding a slide on cost-effectiveness or value proposition. Not price, but how it compares to current standard of care in terms of outcomes and efficiency.

That's a good point, but I want to be careful here. Do we have approved health economic data? I don't want to make claims about cost-effectiveness without solid evidence. Let me check with medical affairs on what we can say.

I've reviewed the deck too. The safety data section is thorough. From a sales angle, I think we should add a slide on implementation—how clinicians would actually integrate this into their workflow. That's often a barrier.
Good idea. I can add a slide on implementation and training requirements. That ties into the education piece and shows we've thought through the practical side.
The deck looks good overall. I'd just suggest making sure the slide titles are clear and punchy. Clinicians are busy and we want them to follow the narrative quickly.

Will do. I'll tighten up the titles and make sure each slide has a clear takeaway. I'll have an updated version ready by tomorrow EOD with the contraindications expansion, implementation slide, and refined titles.

Great. Once you have the updated deck, I'll send it to regulatory affairs for review. In the meantime, let's start on the sales script. I've drafted a standard call structure and some objection responses. I'll share that in a separate message.

Here's the draft sales script and objection guide (A3). It includes opening, needs assessment, key messages and closing. I've documented the top 10 objections we typically hear and compliant responses for each. Please review and let me know if anything feels off or if we're missing common objections.

I've reviewed the script. The structure is solid and the objection responses are well-reasoned. One thing: I'd suggest adding a section on how to position the device as complementary to existing workflows rather than disruptive. That's a common concern from clinicians.

Good work on this. The objection responses are practical. I'd add one more: 'What's the learning curve?' That comes up a lot. Also, I think we should include a section on how to handle requests for additional clinical data or references. Clinicians often want to dig deeper.
The script feels natural. I like that it's not too rigid. One suggestion: add a section on follow-up steps. After the initial call, what's the next move? That helps clinicians understand the process.
I've reviewed it. Looks comprehensive. I'd just make sure we're clear on what we can and can't say about off-label uses. That's critical for compliance.

Good points all around. Let me incorporate these: add the learning curve objection, clarify how to handle requests for additional data, add a follow-up section, and emphasise the complementary positioning. I'll also make sure the compliance language is crystal clear. Updated version by EOD tomorrow.
Perfect. Once you have both the updated deck and script, I'll review them together to make sure the messaging is consistent. Then we can send to regulatory for approval.
Agreed. Let's plan for regulatory review by end of week. Once we get their sign-off, we can lock D3 and D4—final structure and key messages for the deck, and approval of the script for pilot use.
Works for me. Once the script is approved, I can start doing some dry runs with the team to make sure everyone is comfortable with the messaging.
Good idea. I can also do a quick training session on the deck—walk through the key messages and how to handle common questions. That'll help everyone feel confident.
Perfect. Let's schedule that training for next week once we have regulatory approval. I'll send out the updated deck and script by EOD tomorrow for your final review before we submit to regulatory.
Sounds good. I'm ready to start using the script once it's approved.
I'll make sure the CRM is set up to track all script usage and feedback. That'll help us refine it as we go.

Great. I've just uploaded the updated deck and script to A2 and A3. Both are ready for regulatory review. I'm marking D3 and D4 as decided pending regulatory sign-off. Once we get approval, we can move forward with training and pilot execution.

threads.thread_goal: Lock the digital outreach plan and webinar schedule.

messages.text: I've drafted the digital outreach plan for the new device (A4). It outlines our social media and email strategy, including channels, posting frequency and content themes. I've also sketched out topics for 3-5 pilot webinars targeting our key accounts. The plan is ready for feedback. Let me know if the channels and content approach make sense from a sales perspective, and if the webinar topics align with what clinicians want to hear.

Thanks for getting this out. I've reviewed the plan. The channels look good—LinkedIn and email are the right mix for reaching clinicians. One question: what's the cadence for posts? And do we have a content calendar drafted?

Good question. I'm proposing twice-weekly LinkedIn posts and weekly emails during the pilot. The content calendar is in the plan—it covers clinical education, case studies, and implementation tips. I can adjust the cadence if that feels too aggressive or too light.

Twice weekly on LinkedIn might be a lot. Clinicians get bombarded with content. I'd suggest once weekly with really high-quality posts. And the weekly emails are good. Also, are we planning to segment the email list by account or specialty?
That's fair. Once weekly on LinkedIn is probably smarter. And yes, I was planning to segment emails by specialty and account. That way we can tailor the content to what's relevant for each group.
I like the webinar topics. 'Clinical outcomes and safety data' and 'Implementation best practices' are exactly what my contacts want to hear about. What dates are you thinking for the first webinars?

I'm thinking we start with the first webinar in two weeks. That gives us time to get the deck and script approved and do a dry run. I'm proposing four webinars over the pilot period, spaced two weeks apart. Does that timeline work for everyone?
Two weeks out works. I'll make sure the CRM is set up to track webinar registrations and attendance. That'll help us measure engagement.

Four webinars over the pilot period is good. That gives us enough touchpoints without overwhelming the accounts. Let's confirm the specific dates and target accounts for each webinar. I'll coordinate with the account owners to make sure we're hitting the right people.
I can help with that. I know the best times to reach my accounts. Some prefer morning webinars, others prefer afternoon. Let me know the proposed dates and I'll confirm availability.
I'll draft a proposed schedule with dates and times for each webinar, mapped to the target accounts. I'll send that out by tomorrow so we can lock it in.
Good. Once we have the dates, I can start reaching out to my contacts to gauge interest and get them on the calendar.

Overall, the digital outreach plan looks solid. I'd suggest we also include a section on how we'll measure success—click-through rates, webinar attendance, lead generation, etc. That ties into the KPI tracking we're setting up.
Good point. I'll add a measurement section to A4 that outlines what we'll track and how we'll evaluate the effectiveness of each channel. That'll help us optimise as we go.
I can help set up the tracking in the CRM. We can pull reports on email opens, clicks, webinar registrations, etc.
Perfect. I'll have the updated plan with the measurement section and proposed webinar schedule ready by EOD tomorrow. Then we can lock in D5 and D6.

Great. Once we have the updated plan and schedule, I'll send both to the marketing manager and regulatory affairs for sign-off. We need to make sure the digital content is compliant before we start posting.
Agreed. Once we have regulatory approval, we can start the email campaign and schedule the LinkedIn posts. I'll help draft some of the content based on the sales perspective.

That would be really helpful. Sales insights will make the content more practical and relevant. Let's plan a quick sync once we have regulatory approval to align on the first batch of posts and emails.
I'm ready to start reaching out to accounts once the webinar schedule is locked. Just let me know the dates and I'll get them confirmed.

Will do. I'll have the schedule ready by EOD tomorrow. In the meantime, I'm marking D5 (select digital channels and content types) and D6 (confirm webinar dates and target accounts) as pending final approval. Once we have the updated plan, we can lock these in.
Perfect. Let's aim to have everything approved and ready to launch by end of next week. That gives us time to execute the webinars and digital outreach during the pilot period.

threads.thread_goal: Align on CRM logging, KPIs and reporting expectations.

messages.text: I've prepared the KPI tracking template (A6) and a draft CRM logging process (A8). The template includes fields for account, stage, value, next step and outcome. The CRM process outlines which fields are required for each new device interaction and how to log them. I've also created a pre-call compliance checklist (A5) to make sure reps are using approved materials. Please review and let me know if we're missing anything or if the process feels too rigid.

Good work. I've reviewed the template and process. The KPI fields look comprehensive. One question: are we tracking pipeline value separately from closed deals? And how are we defining 'stage'—is it discovery, demo, proposal, etc.?

Good questions. Yes, we're tracking pipeline value separately. And for stage, I'm proposing: initial contact, needs assessment, product demo, proposal, negotiation, closed won, closed lost. Does that work?

That stage progression makes sense. One thing: I'd add a 'follow-up scheduled' stage. Sometimes we have a good conversation but need to circle back after the clinician has had time to think. That's an important milestone.
Good point. I'll add 'follow-up scheduled' as a stage. That captures the momentum and shows we're staying engaged.
I've reviewed the CRM process. It's clear and not too burdensome. One question: how often do we need to update the CRM? Daily? Weekly?

That's a good question. I'd suggest we log interactions within 24 hours of the call or meeting. That keeps the data fresh without being too onerous. And we can do a weekly review to make sure everything is current.
I can set up automated reminders in the CRM to prompt reps to log interactions. That'll help with compliance. I'll also run a weekly report to flag any missing entries.

Perfect. That'll help keep the data clean. Now, on the KPIs themselves: I'm proposing we track leads generated, demos scheduled, proposals sent, and closed deals. We'll also track engagement metrics like email opens and webinar attendance. Does that cover what we need?
That's a solid set of KPIs. I'd also suggest tracking 'objections raised' and 'objections overcome.' That'll help us understand what's working and what needs refinement in the script.
Great idea. I'll add those to the template. That'll give us real-time feedback on the messaging and help us iterate quickly.

I've looked at the compliance checklist (A5). It's thorough. I like that it reminds reps to use only approved materials. One suggestion: add a section on what to do if a clinician asks about off-label uses. That's a tricky situation.

Good catch. I'll add guidance on off-label questions. The standard response should be to acknowledge the question, explain that we can only discuss approved indications, and offer to connect them with medical affairs if they want to explore the science further.
That's the right approach. I'll make sure the CRM has a field to flag off-label questions so we can track them and share with medical affairs.

Good. Now let's talk about reporting. I'm thinking we do a weekly summary of KPIs—leads, demos, proposals, closed deals, and engagement metrics. We can share that in the channel every Monday. Does that work?
Weekly reporting makes sense. I can pull the data from the CRM and create a summary. I'll also include any notable feedback or objections that came up during the week.
That's good. Weekly visibility will help us spot trends and adjust quickly if something isn't working.
Overall, the process looks solid. I'm ready to start logging interactions once we get the CRM set up. Just need a quick walkthrough on how to use it.
I'll schedule a training session on the CRM process for the team. I'll walk through the required fields, how to log interactions, and how to use the reports. That'll be next week.

Perfect. Let me summarise where we are: we're tracking leads, demos, proposals, closed deals, engagement metrics, objections, and off-label questions. We're logging interactions within 24 hours. We're doing weekly KPI reviews. And we have a compliance checklist to ensure reps use approved materials. I'm marking D7 and D8 as decided.
Great. I'll have the updated templates ready by EOD tomorrow with all the feedback incorporated. Then we can share them with the team and get started on the pilot.
I'll get the CRM configured and ready for the training session. Should be good to go by next week.
Excellent. We're on track. Let's reconvene next week to confirm everything is set up and ready for the pilot launch.

threads.thread_goal: Share pilot results, feedback and decide on broader rollout.

messages.text: We've completed the pilot phase with our eight target accounts. I've compiled the results and lessons learned in the post-pilot report (A7). Here's a quick summary: we generated 24 leads, scheduled 18 demos, sent 12 proposals, and closed 3 deals. Engagement on digital channels was strong—email open rates averaged 42% and webinar attendance was solid. The feedback from clinicians was very positive on the educational approach. I've also pulled the KPI data from A6 and summarised the key insights. Let me know what you think and if we should adjust anything before broader rollout.

Excellent results. 24 leads and 3 closed deals in the pilot is a strong start. The engagement metrics are impressive too. Let me review the full report and I'll share my thoughts. One quick question: what were the main objections we encountered?

The top objections were: 'What's the learning curve?' (6 instances), 'How does this compare to current standard of care?' (5 instances), and 'What's the cost?' (4 instances). The sales script handled most of these well, but we did need to refine the response on cost-effectiveness. I've documented all the feedback in the report.

Those are the objections I expected. The learning curve response in the script worked well—clinicians appreciated the honesty about training time. On cost, I think we need to emphasise value and outcomes rather than just price. That's where the health economic data would help.

I agree. The script is solid overall. The objection responses felt natural and didn't sound canned. I'd say we're ready to use it for broader rollout, maybe with a small tweak on the cost-effectiveness angle.

I've reviewed the CRM data from the pilot. The logging process worked well—we captured all the key interactions and feedback. The weekly reports were clean and easy to read. I'd say the process is ready for broader use.

Great feedback. Let me pull together the key learnings from the pilot: the educational approach resonates with clinicians, the script is effective with minor tweaks, the digital outreach is driving engagement, and the CRM process is working well. I think we're in good shape for broader rollout.

I agree. The pilot validated the approach. Now, for broader rollout, I'm thinking we expand to the next tier of accounts—maybe 15-20 more. We'll use the same script and materials, but we should incorporate the learnings on cost-effectiveness messaging. That ties into D4—do we keep the script as is or update it?

I'd suggest we update the script with a stronger cost-effectiveness section. We have the health economic data now, so we can back up the value proposition. That'll address the cost objection more effectively.
I can work with you on that. Let me draft an updated cost-effectiveness section for the script and we'll get it reviewed by medical affairs before we roll it out.
Good plan. Once the script is updated, I'll do a dry run with the new messaging to make sure it feels natural.
I'll also update the CRM to track cost-effectiveness objections separately so we can monitor how the new messaging performs.

Perfect. So here's the plan: we update the script with cost-effectiveness messaging, get it approved by medical affairs, and then roll out to the next tier of accounts. We'll also expand the digital outreach to reach more accounts. I'm marking D4 as updated—we're keeping the script but refining it based on pilot feedback.
I'll also update the educational deck with any refinements based on pilot feedback. The structure was solid, but there were a few questions about implementation that we can address more clearly.
Good idea. The implementation section was helpful in the pilot. Let's make sure that's crystal clear in the updated deck.
I'm ready to start reaching out to the next tier of accounts. Just let me know when the updated materials are ready.

I'll coordinate the rollout. Let's aim to have the updated script and deck approved by end of week, and we'll start outreach to the next tier of accounts next week. That gives us momentum while the pilot results are fresh.
I'll have the updated script and deck ready for review by EOD Thursday. That gives us time for medical affairs to review and approve before we launch next week.
I'll prepare the next tier account list and make sure the CRM is ready to track the expanded rollout. We'll also continue the weekly KPI reporting so we can monitor progress.

Excellent. We've validated the approach with the pilot and we're ready to scale. The pilot results show strong engagement and early traction. Let's keep the momentum going and expand to the next tier of accounts. I'll send out a summary of the pilot results and the rollout plan to stakeholders.
Great work everyone. The pilot was a success and I'm confident in the approach. Let's keep executing and refining as we go.
Thanks. I'll have the full post-pilot report (A7) and updated materials ready by EOD Thursday. Looking forward to the next phase.
